status_detail: Gallup City Council agenda on 2026-04-28 included a Teraplex presentation for a potential project at Gallup Tradeport and an effluent option agreement. Official agenda says Teraplex intends to acquire about 330 acres in the city and adjacent properties and buy up to 109,500,000 gallons/year of effluent for industrial/commercial uses including a data center; later local reporting/podcast quotes Greg Thompson describing five to ten buildings and total capacity of 1 GW planned over five years, but land acquisition/permits were still prospective.
notes: Capacity is from KGLP/local-reporting quote of developer presentation, not in the city agenda text. City agreement terms included 3-year option exercise, 4-year property purchase deadline, and 5-year construction-commencement termination trigger.

project_name: Mescalero Apache Telecom Administrative Office and Data Center
aliases: MATI Administrative Office and Data Center
status_detail: New Mexico DoIT reported FCC Commissioner Olivia Trusty visited MATI's new $44 million Administrative Office and Data Center; MATI General Manager Godfrey Enjady gave a tour inside the new data center, which opened in April 2026. Connect New Mexico listed a ribbon cutting for the MATI Data Center and Office Building on 2026-05-06 at 75 Carrizo Canyon Road, Mescalero, NM.
notes: This is a tribal telecom/broadband data center, not a hyperscale AI campus. Separate Otero County Commission materials on 2026-03-12 authorized preliminary feasibility assessment/outreach for possible data center and advanced energy development but did not identify a submitted named project.

project_name: Otero County data center and advanced energy development feasibility assessment
status_detail: Otero County Commission agenda item 28/2026 for 2026-03-12 requested authorization for the County Attorney to conduct preliminary feasibility assessment and stakeholder outreach for data center and advanced energy infrastructure development in Otero County, including outreach to landowners, developers and advanced energy companies; no specific data center developer/site approval was identified.
notes: Included under broad net because the county itself initiated feasibility/outreach, but this is not a permit, abatement, land deal, or named project. Local report said no large-scale data center had been approved in Otero County as of May 2026.
